statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is in the low band on observed two-sided overnight rotation with NQ off its session high; a narrow elevated window is flagged around the U.S. cash open and the S&P Global flash PMIs.
recommendation: Conditions are consistent with normal mean-reverting behaviour outside a narrow checkpoint window of 13:30-14:30 UTC (15:30-16:30 Berlin), when the opening auction, the flash PMIs and the EIA crude report cluster. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 rotates two-sided in a narrow overnight band at record levels; Tail held low with a flagged cash-open and flash-PMI window
body: NQ futures are trading near 31,003, about 0.07% below the prior settle of 31,028.5 and in the lower half of an overnight band of roughly 30,983-31,095 (about 0.36%). Price is some 90 points below the session high, so the index is not holding a session extreme and the observed structure is two-sided rotation rather than persistent one-way extension: there is no repeated extension after failed retracements and no shallow-pullback signature. VIX near 14.18, marginally below the prior close of 14.21, confirms a calm volatility backdrop. The multi-day regime is nonetheless a bullish uptrend: the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,732.40 on 22 September, up 0.82% and at the top of its 52-week range, while the Nasdaq Composite set a second consecutive record close at 27,244.28 on a sixth straight advancing session for semiconductors. That aligned regime is a conditional amplifier for the U.S. open, not observed pathological structure, so it is scored into the forecast rather than into current Tail. Cross-asset evidence is mixed rather than aligned: Treasury yields remain elevated, with the 10Y near 4.96% and the 2Y near 4.76% and the effective fed funds rate at 3.88% after the September policy move, which caps valuation expansion in long-duration tech. Crude has fallen for a sixth consecutive session, with WTI near $89-90 and Brent below $100, after Saudi Arabia restarted the East-West pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, Iraq lifted exports above 3 million barrels per day, and U.S. and Iranian officials held reported talks at the UN. That de-escalation impulse reduces the discontinuity channel that has driven this year's tail episodes, although the underlying blockade and Hormuz restrictions remain unresolved and keep a floor under Stress. Tail is therefore held at 12 and Stress eased to 35. The flagged window covers the 13:30 UTC cash open, the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMIs and the 14:30 UTC EIA crude report; conditional Tail peaks at 21 in the 13:00 UTC hour and decays thereafter on the base case of orderly price discovery, with a secondary lift to 17 in the 19:00 UTC power hour. The scheduled Trump-Xi meeting later this week is treated as a headline-risk checkpoint in the forecast, not as an observed driver. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was partial, carried no futures coverage and was about four and a half hours old at assessment time, so it was treated as stale and excluded; this assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, so coverage is continuous with no gap. Tail moved between 10 and 21, with three WATCH hours clustered around the 22 September U.S. cash open (14:00 UTC) and the 18:00-19:00 UTC afternoon, each resolving back into the low band within one to two hours. The trend-up labelling that ran from 20:00 UTC through 01:00 UTC gave way to a normal, range-bound mode from 02:00 UTC onward, with Tail between 10 and 12 and Stress easing from 37 to 33 before firming to 36 into the European morning. Confidence held between 84 and 88 throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band for 22 of the 24 hours and concentrates conditional risk in a single narrow window. Tail rises from 12 to 21 in the 13:00 UTC hour, which contains both the cash open and the flash PMIs, and stays at 20 in the 14:00 UTC hour alongside the EIA crude report; those two slots are the only WATCH hours. Because a record close and a six-session semiconductor streak sit behind the open, opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific conditional amplifier to test, and it is not observed at assessment time. On the base case of orderly price discovery, Tail decays to 17 by 15:00 UTC and 14 by 17:00 UTC, with a secondary rise to 17 in the 19:00 UTC power hour on closing-auction imbalance. The overnight cycle returns to 10-11 with no scheduled U.S. macro release, then firms to 12-13 into Thursday's 12:30 UTC jobless claims and the Trump-Xi meeting. Confidence declines gradually from 87 to 84 as evidence distance from the assessment cutoff grows.
